stm-2026-09-03|1|amending fy27 school bu.allowed: To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate an additional sum of Four Hundred Eighteen Thousand Fifty-Six Dollars and No Cents ($418,056.00) for the FY 27 operating budget for the School Department, or take any other action relative thereto Amending FY27 school budget $418,056.00
stm-2026-09-03|1|amending fy27 school bu.summary: This would add $418,056.00 to the School Department's FY27 operating budget. The School Committee brought it, and the boards' discussion ties it to additional state aid; at Town Meeting the Select Board proposed lowering the amount.

stm-2026-09-03|2|authorization to supple.allowed: To see if the Town will vote to raise and appropriate, or transfer from available funds, a sum of money to supplement the School Department’s Fiscal Year 2027 (FY2027) operating budget, or take any other action relative thereto Authorization to supplement the school department’s fiscal year 2027 operating budget
stm-2026-09-03|2|authorization to supple.summary: This would let the Town set aside an unnamed sum to add to the School Department's FY27 operating budget. Its lead sponsor planned to ask Town Meeting to pass it over, and Town Meeting did, so it was not acted on.

stm-2026-09-03|3|supplement to the lunen.allowed: To see if the Town will vote to transfer a sum of money in the amount of $151,338.38 from Certified Free Cash or available funds to the Lunenburg Public Schools Fiscal Year 2027 Operating Budget for the purpose of supplementing the athletic department budget to reinstate middle school sports as well as provide transportation for student athletes; or take any other action relative thereto Supplement to the Lunenburg Public Schools fiscal year 2027 operating budget $151,338.38
stm-2026-09-03|3|supplement to the lunen.summary: A citizens' petition asking to move $151,338.38 into the schools' FY27 budget to bring back middle school sports and pay for student athletes' transportation. The article's wording does not legally bind how the School Committee spends it, and at Town Meeting the motion proposed taking the money from the Winter Recovery Assistance Program fund.

stm-2026-11-17|10|advisory on stormwater.allowed: advisory on stormwater funding mechanisms   $480,000 -- a year, about: the stormwater program’s cost, as presented by the Stormwater Task Force; not voted $109 -- a year, about, for a single-family home if paid through property taxes, as presented by the Stormwater Task Force; not voted $85 -- a year for a single-family home under the stormwater fee ($85 per unit of paved area), as presented by the Stormwater Task Force; not voted $100 -- the most the fee would be per property for its first three years, as presented by the Stormwater Task Force
stm-2026-11-17|10|advisory on stormwater.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17|10|advisory on stormwater.summary: This is a non-binding question: it asks voters how the town should pay for stormwater permit compliance, through property taxes or a fee based on paved area. The Stormwater Task Force presented the program as costing about $480,000 a year, or about $109 a year for a single-family home through taxes versus $85 under the fee, with the fee capped at $100 per property at first. None of those figures has been voted.

stm-2026-11-17|11|continuity of trust fu.allowed: continuity of trust fund administration during vacancy
stm-2026-11-17|11|continuity of trust fu.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17|11|continuity of trust fu.summary: This article, written by the Trust Fund Commission, would set how trust funds keep being administered while a seat on the commission is empty. The Select Board included it, and one member said parts of the draft could override the town charter.

stm-2026-11-17|1|reports of officers and.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17|1|reports of officers and.summary: This is the usual article asking Town Meeting to hear and accept reports from town officers and committees. It involves no money, and the Select Board recommends approval.

stm-2026-11-17|2|defer articles 2 and 3.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17|2|defer articles 2 and 3.summary: This article would defer Articles 2 and 3 to the special town meeting. The Select Board voted to bring it forward; the material gives no other detail and no dollar amount.

stm-2026-11-17|4|transfer to special edu.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17|4|transfer to special edu.summary: The School Committee asks to move $300,000 into the special education reserve fund, taken from free cash if it is certified in time. The Select Board voted to recommend disapproval.

stm-2026-11-17|5|middle high school trac.allowed: middle high school track and field engineering   $195,830 -- the engineering request about $2 million -- the whole track and field project, as estimated from a prior assessment
stm-2026-11-17|5|middle high school trac.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17|5|middle high school trac.summary: The School Committee asks the town to pay $195,830 for engineering and design work on the Middle High School track and field. The superintendent told the Select Board this is for design and engineering only, not construction; the whole project is about $2 million, estimated from a prior assessment. The Select Board most recently voted to defer it.

stm-2026-11-17|6|design and engineering.allowed: design and engineering for accessibility and park improvements
stm-2026-11-17|6|design and engineering.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17|6|design and engineering.summary: This article is about design and engineering work for accessibility and park improvements; no dollar amount appears in the material. The Select Board's notes say it was included to vote it down, but a later approval recommendation is recorded under a stormwater title, so where the board stands is unclear.

stm-2026-11-17|7|take no position on art.allowed: Take no position on Articles 7 and 8 (non-binding straw polls)
stm-2026-11-17|7|take no position on art.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17|7|take no position on art.summary: Articles 7 and 8 are non-binding straw polls, so they decide nothing and only show how voters feel. The Select Board voted to take no position on them.

stm-2026-11-17|9|track and field enginee.allowed: track and field engineering   $195,830 -- the engineering request about $2 million -- the whole track and field project, as estimated from a prior assessment
stm-2026-11-17|9|track and field enginee.from: the boards' discussion, from our notes of the recordings
stm-2026-11-17|9|track and field enginee.summary: The School Committee asks the town to pay $195,830 for engineering and bid-ready design documents for rebuilding the Lunenburg Middle High School track and turf field. The whole project is about $2 million, estimated from a prior assessment, and the request covers design work, not construction. The Select Board voted to defer this article.
